name: Editorial Design
visualIdentity: Explicitly magazine/book-like: headlines, short copy, images and annotations arranged on a consistent grid, with purposeful serif–sans-serif pairing. Reveal in reading order; use crops, grouped movement and layout changes rather than sliding a whole page.
suitableUses: Suitable for article-like narratives, feature stories, case studies, product explainers and data journalism. Inferred fit for video or interactive HTML when hierarchy and reading time matter. Optional motion patterns suit pinned hero recomposition, card stacks, chapter handoffs, carousels or staged storytelling only when their content and geometry fit.
limitations: Avoid hierarchy changes without explanatory value, crops that lose key details, unsafe text placement and motion that interrupts reading. Stacks must not hide needed copy or provenance; carousels may not suit long-form reading or simultaneous comparison. Motion references are optional, not style requirements.
palette: Suggested fallback only: paper background #FAF5EA, dark type #252A30, vermilion accent #A84235; three discrete tokens, no gradient. Exact task, brand or approved reference colors take precedence and retain roles and asset colors. Check actual composited contrast; do not recolor assets or add hues automatically.
motionAndInteraction: Measure fonts and build a shared headline, body and image grid. Use masks, grouped movement and layout reflow with reading holds. For HTML, scroll may drive pinned or staged states; support coherent reverse progress, release behavior, accessible navigation and reduced motion. Video must use authored, deterministic composition-time states, not live input. Keep one owner per animated property and verify direct and backward seeks.
audio: Unspecified as a fixed style rule. Suggest music, narration, effects, ambience or silence from the topic and requirements; honor supplied choices, preserve speech and reading comprehension, and synchronize and mix through the render pipeline.
assetRequirements: Use supplied copy, images and fonts; preload and measure actual fonts. Crop raster assets non-destructively, preserve source identity, essential context and motion margins, and record crop parameters if needed. Gallery work requires real images and captions; do not assume photography or invent assets. Captions need deliberate custom UI with PhotoSwipe.
combinations: Can stand alone. Optional style-024 margin notes add a restrained handwritten editor voice: vermilion marker, dark type, at most two notes per spread, never over body copy. Optional style-097 chart sidebars use the grid and type, highlight only the series in vermilion, and require captions and supplied data sources. Avoid dashboard walls and unsourced numbers.
productionApproach: HTML/CSS and SVG are the suggested visual tools for typography, grid, masks and scalable graphics; choose only what the scene needs. GSAP is the primary suggested seekable motion timeline; Motion is optional and requires verified time synchronization. PhotoSwipe is only for an interactive image lightbox, not an inline carousel or video engine; Cropper.js is optional crop authoring. HyperFrames owns video assembly, timing, sync, checks and export; use Remotion only if unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a requirement, recording the reason. Select visual and motion methods before pipeline; do not treat pipeline defaults as art direction.
